Q: gradle Unexpected lock protocol found in lock file. Expected 3, found 0 A:

If you're getting this error in current Android Studio versions (I'm currently using Android Studio Otter 3 Feature Drop | 2025.2.3), I couldn't solve it by invalidating the cache or deleting the .gradle folder. I changed my Gradle version from 9.1.0 to 9.2.0 in the Project Structure section of the settings. This solved the problem.

Q: What cybersecurity skills should beginners focus on first? A:

I'd recommend learning in this order:

  • Start with an operating system like Linux or Windows and understand how it works.

  • Learn networking fundamentals to see how devices communicate and how attacks happen.

  • Pick up basic Python to automate simple tasks and understand scripts.

  • Study web security fundamentals and practice in safe lab environments.

  • Earn an entry-level certification to validate your knowledge and improve your job prospects.

Focus on mastering one step before moving to the next the fundamentals will make everything else much easier.

Q: Automatically Parse a Website A:

Scrapy is a good tool designed for this. Depending on how the webpages are rendered, you may or may not need an additional tool like Selenium. Submit or "select" buttons are often just links that can be followed using HTML requests, without an additional browser emulation tool. If you could post some of the sample HTML we could give you more specifics.

Q: How can I build an AI automation workflow that extracts email data, stores it in a CRM, sends follow-up messages without creating duplicate records? A:

That makes sense dedup logic should live in middleware, not the AI layer, so it survives a vendor or front-end swap.

On identifying customers uniquely: name, email, and phone are a solid starting point, but I'll dig into the actual data to see if those alone are reliable (e.g. shared emails/phones across customers, name variations, typos). I'll check with the team and run some test cases against real records before locking in the matching logic.

And good call on using AI to help write the middleware I'll treat any generated code the same as a contributor's PR: review it line by line and test it against edge cases before it touches production.

Q: how to connect to a oracle db in bash script? A:

On *nix systems, this will create a csv stream of results to standard out:

java -Djava.security.egd=file///dev/urandom -jar jdbcsql.jar -d oracledb_SID -h $host -p 1521 -U some_username -m oracle -P "$PW" -f excel -s "," "$1"

Note that adding the -Djava.security.egd=file///dev/urandom increases performance greatly

Windows commands are similar: see http://jdbcsql.sourceforge.net/
